To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the boundary value problems for the Dirichlet, Neumann and mixed problems for the Helmholtz equation and for Maxwell’s equations in Lipschitz domains are well-posed in the L P -norm with L P -estimations for the nontangetial maximal functions with 1 < p < ∞.
the Maxwell system is well-posed in L p for p near 2 in Lipschitz domains, with mixed boundary conditions.

the boundary value problem for the mixed Dirichlet-Neumann problem for the Maxwell system in a Lipschit domain is well-posed in L p for p near 2, with p depending only on the Lipschitz constant for ∂Ω and the size of the angles at which ∂Ω meets itself.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the boundary value problems for the Helmholtz equation in the plane and in space, and the Maxwell equations in space.
the study of the boundary value problems for the time-harmonic Maxwell equations in a bounded Lipschitz domain in R 3 with mixed boundary conditions.
the analysis and numerical approximation of Maxwell’s equations in a bounded domain Ω with mixed boundary conditions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Maxwell system is a “good” boundary value problem for the nontangetial maximal function, and that the tangential component of the electric or magnetic field is “good” boundary data for this problem.

the mixed boundary-value problem for the Maxwell system in a Lipschitch domain in ℝ 3 is well-posed in L 2 (Ω) when the tangential components are prescribed on two disjoint, relatively closed subsets ∑ e and of ∑ h of the boundary, provided that ∑ e and are sufficiently smooth and that ∂Ω ∖ ( ∑ e ∪ ∑ h ) is sufficiently small in a sense that will be made precise below.
, in the three-dimensional case, the boundary-value problem with mixed boundary conditions is well-posed in the L P -sense for any p ∈ (1,∞), provided that the boundary data are sufficiently smooth.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the Maxwell equations with mixed boundary conditions can be solved with the same regularity theory as the Laplace equation.
the mixed boundary value problem is as well-posed as the Dirichlet problem for the Maxwell system, in a wide range of Sobolev spaces.
the boundary conditions are well-posed when the domain is smooth enough and when the boundary conditions are “sufficiently regular”.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the boundary conditions are not the main obstacle for well-posedness.
the well-posedness of this problem is not dependent on the geometry of the boundary of the domain, but rather on the geometry of ∑ e and of ∑ h.
, when the boundary data is in a certain sense small in L 2, the solution of the mixed problem can be controlled by the boundary data, and the solution is small in L 6.
